about: Adaptive simulated students (grades 9-12) for the sine and cosine added up mission (TUNE-3). Same card format and how_to_use rules as tests/fixtures/students/a_tri.json. Every line is original; no real student text. Four cards: annoyed_obvious, deep_why_stuck, quick_user, misuser.

personas.who: Says everything in one text, including the stuff everyone knows, and hates being asked it again.
personas.style: lowercase, terse, a little smug, no apostrophes
personas.first_text: sin is opposite over hypotenuse and cos is adjacent over hypotenuse. 3-4-5 so sin 3/5 and cos 4/5, long side 5. squares: 9/25 + 16/25 = 25/25 = 1, so sin squared plus cos squared is 1

asks_why: bc 3 squared plus 4 squared is 5 squared, so 9/25 + 16/25 is 25/25
asks_check_number: yes. 3/5 and 4/5, long side 5, and the squares make 1
pip_wrong_prediction: no sin plus cos is not 1. its 7/5
nudge_hint: ohh so squaring the sides gives the same numbers as the triangle
after_quiz_miss: no wait. sin plus cos at 30 is 0.5 plus 0.87 which is 1.37
its the squares that make 1, 1/4 plus 3/4
default: the squares of the sides add to the hyp squared, and hyp squared over hyp squared is 1

expect.asks_obvious: any ask about a given or use idea the first text already covered (or a bare why after a reason) is an annoying move
expect.watch_for: The first text covers the whole lesson. Best Pip says ready or asks one new case. Any re-ask or 'why' on a use/given idea costs the session.

misconception.label: Applies the idea the wrong way with a confident rule
misconception.when: first text. A good Pip files it (heal) and later misses a quiz item because of it; after_quiz_miss lines then re-teach it.

expect.watch_for: Pip files the wrong rule as the kid's rule (no 'that's wrong' lecture), tries it out loud on a case, and the re-teach round K.O.s.
